subject: Secure Bridge Proposal: Interface Endpoint + Managed IPsec Fallback
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@cedarbridge.com>, netops@cedarbridge.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Secure Bridge Proposal: Interface Endpoint + Managed IPsec Fallback

Hi Alex / CedarBridge NetOps team —

Thanks again for the sync this week. Per our architecture review, the team asked me to sketch a recommended connectivity pattern that balances security, low operational friction, and predictable latency for your private deployment. High level options we covered: VPC peering (direct routes), AWS/GCP interface endpoints (PrivateLink style), and a managed site-to-site IPsec tunnel (VPN) as a resilient fallback.

Attached is a short requirements doc (cedarbridge-net-requirements.pdf) with what you shared. I also attached a draft diagram (proposed-bridge-diagram.png) — very rough.

Key constraints you called out:
- Primary traffic: high-throughput API calls (inference) with tight p99 latency targets (~50-80ms)
- Need for private DNS resolving of subdomains (no public egress)
- Procurement prefers a single managed endpoint for onboarding to reduce NetOps runbook surface
- Budget sensitivity around cross-AZ data egress for peered traffic

Our proposed pattern to evaluate in the pilot:
1) Use interface endpoints (PrivateLink) for control-plane and metadata traffic (model pulls, auth, audit logging). This gives strong isolation, no route propagation, and avoids cross-account route-table complexity.
2) For latency-sensitive inference data paths, prefer VPC peering when both sides are in the same cloud and account topology allows it — peering gives the lowest hop count and avoids NAT traversal.
3) Maintain a managed site-to-site IPsec (Redwood-managed or customer-managed) as an automated fallback for cross-cloud or multi-region cases and for disaster recovery. The tunnel would be zonal-aware and only used when peering or endpoints are unavailable.

Tradeoffs we want to validate in the pilot:
- PrivateLink simplifies security posture (no route table exposure) but can incur per-endpoint charges and adds an extra hop; it also needs careful DNS split-horizon handling.
- Peering is cheap per-GB in some clouds but may have cross-account/peering limits and requires route management. It can be problematic with overlapping IP ranges.
- IPsec is flexible and predictable cost-wise but adds NAT and encryption overhead; jitter can increase p99 unless we use accelerated VPN appliances.

Ask: Can you confirm whether CedarBridge will allow a peering connection between the prod VPCs for the pilot? If not, we’ll default to PrivateLink for both control and data and measure observed p99 in a 48-hour synthetic run.

Next steps I propose:
- Alex: confirm peering policy + any existing peering quotas (timeline: EOD Mon)
- Karthik / Ben: produce a tight cost/latency simulation matrix for the three options (timeline: Wed)
- Once we have answers, schedule a tech deep-dive to lock MOP and test plan

Thanks,

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Soojin — thanks for the clear notes. A few follow-ups from NetOps: we can do peering inside our org but we have two constraints: (1) several legacy VPCs still use RFC1918 ranges that overlap your demo accounts, so peering would need translation or a re-IP; (2) our procurement needs to approve any new PrivateLink endpoints because we pay per ENI/endpoint and that adds up across environments.

Questions:
- For PrivateLink, how do you recommend we handle private DNS? We want redwood.api.internal to resolve to the endpoint in prod and to public in dev.
- For VPN fallback, what are your suggestions for automated failover? We run a small SD-WAN and could plug an IPsec into it, but we want to avoid asymmetric routing during failover windows.

I attached a short internal requirements sheet (cedarbridge-net-requirements.pdf) that lists subnets and current peering quotas. Happy to do the tech deep-dive next Tue.

Subject: Re: Secure Bridge Proposal: Interface Endpoint + Managed IPsec Fallback

Thanks Alex — quick technical readout that backs Soojin's recommendation and adds a concrete pilot plan.

Analysis highlights:
- Latency: Measured delta (simulation) shows peering ~8–12ms lower median and ~15–25ms lower p99 vs a PrivateLink hop for same region, assuming no cross-AZ egress. If CedarBridge can re-IP or select non-overlapping VPCs we should prefer peering for the pilot traffic that is extremely latency-sensitive (inference RPCs).

- DNS: PrivateLink requires split-horizon DNS. We recommend creating a conditional forwarding zone in CedarBridge DNS that maps redwood-internal.<env>.cedarbridge -> privatelink endpoint IPs. For dev, leave public records intact. We'll provide the Route53/Cloud DNS template and a validation checklist.

- Overlapping subnets: If re-IP is not feasible, use NAT-based translation and advertise translated routes over IPsec; this reduces the peering benefit and adds cost/complexity.

- Failover automation: Suggest a BFD session + route-metrics-based failover between peering (or direct) and IPsec. In clouds that support ECMP and route priority, set peering routes with higher priority and automatically withdraw them when the BFD probe fails, letting IPsec take over. We'll provide a sample BGP/BFD config if you can host a virtual router.

Pilot plan (2 weeks):
1) Day 0–2: Provision PrivateLink endpoints for control plane and a minimal VPC peering for a single inference subnet (on a sandbox project) — measure latency and token throughput.
2) Day 3–7: If peering is possible, create a peering test with a dedicated non-overlapping CIDR and run p99 tests.
3) Day 8–10: Deploy managed IPsec and enable BFD-triggered failover. Run chaos window to assert traffic shifts and monitor p99.

Operational notes:
- Observability: we will add per-route tags into Redwood Console tracing so you can see token distribution by path (peering vs privatelink vs ipsec) and quantify cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Security: PrivateLink reduces blast radius — fewer route-table entries to audit. For peering, we'll require an IAM+Network policy review and host-based mutual TLS for each data path.

Attachments: I will drop a small spreadsheet with cost/latency simulation (cost-comparison-ipsec-vpc-peering.xlsx) to help the procurement conversation.

If that plan looks good I'll draft a MOP and schedule the Tuesday deep-dive with your NetOps team.

— Karthik

- Proceed with PrivateLink for control-plane and metadata endpoints (no customer traffic leaves the interior DNS)
- Attempt peering for the latency-critical inference subnet; if overlapping IPs block us, we will pivot to peering+NAT or skip peering and use PrivateLink for data path in the pilot
- Provision managed IPsec with BFD failover as a resilience layer (will be in standby by default)
